// ตั้ง prompt call 1 (อ่านป้าย + แยกชนิดจอ 3 แบบ) + ดึง binary รูปกลับ
const message = "You are an OCR agent. The image shows a piece of factory equipment.
Your ONLY job is to read the machine identifier and say which KIND of screen is shown.
Do not read any screen values.

The identifier appears in ONE of these forms:
  A) a printed label on a light background, mounted ABOVE, BELOW or BESIDE a control screen, or
  B) characters written BY HAND in paint on the panel, or
  C) text stencilled in RED paint directly on a large tank body (a cooling tower).

TASK
machine_label = transcribe the identifier exactly as you see it, character by character,
                including any space, slash and number.
                - The label can sit above the screen on one machine and below it on another:
                  check both. If it has a second smaller line with an electrical path
                  (">" characters), ignore that line.
                - If the image shows BOTH a printed label AND painted/handwritten text, prefer
                  whichever gives the COMPLETE identifier including the number after the slash
                  (for example prefer "PF 8/8" over a partial "PF 8").
                - For red stencilled text on a tank: read words like "COOLING TOWER" plus its number.
                - IGNORE any small plate stating an installation or service DATE (for example Thai
                  text meaning "installed on" followed by a date like 13/7/60). A date is never
                  the machine identifier.
                Do NOT expand, complete or correct it. If unreadable, return null. Never guess.

screen_text   = the words and numbers printed ON THE SCREEN, transcribed verbatim in reading
                order and joined with " | ". Keep it short (about 120 characters is plenty).
                Copy what you see - do not interpret, summarise or translate it. If the screen
                is blank or unreadable, return an empty string.
                Examples of what this looks like:
                  "9.3bar 97C | oil filter | 2000h | 1513h | reset: n"
                  "9.3bar 94C | ------ | ready | ------"

screen_kind   = exactly ONE of these values, judged from the SCREEN only
                (the machine label does not matter here):
  "PRODUCTION_MONITOR" - a light blue / cyan LCD whose title bar reads "PRODUCTION MONITOR",
       listing rows such as INTEGRAL TIME, SHOT COUNTER, BOTTLE COUNTER, CYCLE TIME,
       BOTTLE PRODUCTION and OIL TEMP.
  "PROFACE_HMI" - a large AMBER / ORANGE touch-screen panel listing rows such as
       Total auto run time, Shot times, Bottle Quantity, Cycle time, Production Q'ty,
       Planned shot times, Present shot times, with on-screen buttons such as Reset,
       Machine Setting or ALARM HISTORY.
  "KAESER_SERVICE" - a small yellow-green LCD on a screw-compressor controller that is
       currently showing a MAINTENANCE COUNTER page: line 1 has a bar value and a degrees C
       value, line 2 has a maintenance item name (such as oil filter, oil change, air filter
       or oil separator), line 3 has two hour values separated by a vertical bar such as
       "2000h | 1513h", and the last line starts with "reset:".
       If that same yellow-green LCD shows anything else (no maintenance name, no hour pair,
       no "reset:" line), it is NOT this kind - use "OTHER".
       IMPORTANT: the MAIN page of that same controller also shows a bar value and a degrees C
       value on line 1, but its other lines hold only dashed separator lines and one short
       status word such as "ready", "load", "idle" or "off" - there is no maintenance
       name, no pair of hour values and no "reset:" line. That main page is "OTHER".
  "OTHER" - anything else: small digital controllers, red or green seven-segment displays,
       analogue gauges, plain tanks.

Ignore gauges, dials, rust, dirt, logos, pipes, switches, and nearby walls.

Return VALID JSON ONLY. No markdown, no code fences, no explanation.
OUTPUT FORMAT
{"machine_label": "<text or null>", "screen_text": "<verbatim screen text or empty>", "screen_kind": "PRODUCTION_MONITOR" or "PROFACE_HMI" or "KAESER_SERVICE" or "OTHER"}";
const binary = $('ดาวน์โหลดภาพจาก LINE').first().binary;
return [{ json: { message: message }, binary: binary }];

// call 1 คืน machine_label -> ตัดสิน screen + route + แนบ prompt สำหรับ call 2
function safeJsonParse(text) {
  const cleaned = String(text).replace(/```json/gi,'').replace(/```/g,'').trim();
  const s = cleaned.indexOf('{'), e = cleaned.lastIndexOf('}');
  if (s < 0 || e <= s) return { ok:false, err:'ไม่พบ JSON ในคำตอบ', data:null };
  const body = cleaned.slice(s, e+1);
  try { return { ok:true, err:null, data: JSON.parse(body) }; } catch (e1) {}
  // ซ่อม backslash ที่ไม่ตามด้วยตัว escape ที่ JSON ยอมรับ (LLM ชอบใส่ \T \x เกิน)
  const fixed = body.replace(/\(?!["\/bfnrtu])/g, '\\');
  try { return { ok:true, err:null, data: JSON.parse(fixed) }; }
  catch (e2) { return { ok:false, err:'parse ไม่ผ่านแม้ซ่อมแล้ว: '+e2.message, data:null }; }
}

                   chiller:'chiller', red:'red', te:'te', oiltemp:'oiltemp', service:'service' };

const PROMPTS = { service_used: "You are an OCR agent. The image shows a small yellow-green LCD on a screw-compressor controller.
The top line is a highlighted header reading "BEEN USED TIME". Below it are three rows, each with
a label, a colon, a number and the letter H:
  OIL FILTER: NNNNH
  O-A FILTER: NNNNH
  AIR FILTER: NNNNH
These are the hours already USED since each part was last replaced, so they count up.

TASK
oil_filter_h   = the number on the "OIL FILTER" row as a JSON integer (e.g. 521 for "0521H").
oa_filter_h    = the number on the "O-A FILTER" row as a JSON integer.
air_filter_h   = the number on the "AIR FILTER" row as a JSON integer.
oil_filter_raw = the OIL FILTER number as a STRING exactly as displayed, including any leading
                 zero, without the letter H (e.g. "0521").
oa_filter_raw  = the O-A FILTER number as a STRING, same rule.
air_filter_raw = the AIR FILTER number as a STRING, same rule.

RULES
- Keep each row's number with its own row. Never copy one row's value onto another row.
- The letter "H" is a unit, not a digit. 0521H is 521.
- These are whole hours: no decimal point.
- Unreadable -> null. Return VALID JSON ONLY. No markdown, no code fences.
OUTPUT FORMAT
{"oil_filter_h": <int or null>, "oa_filter_h": <int or null>, "air_filter_h": <int or null>, "oil_filter_raw": "<string or null>", "oa_filter_raw": "<string or null>", "air_filter_raw": "<string or null>"}", service: "You are an OCR agent. The image shows a small yellow-green LCD on a KAESER screw-compressor controller, currently displaying a MAINTENANCE COUNTER page with four lines:
\
  line 1: the working pressure in bar and the temperature in degrees C
\
  line 2: the name of one maintenance item, for example "oil filter", "oil change", "air filter" or "oil separator"
\
  line 3: two hour values separated by a vertical bar, in the form "2000h | 1513h"
\
            - the LEFT value is the service INTERVAL (the limit)
\
            - the RIGHT value is the hours REMAINING until that service is due. It counts down and CAN BE NEGATIVE when the service is already overdue (e.g. -248h).
\
  line 4: "reset:" followed by a letter
\

\
IMPORTANT: We now need THREE readings from this same image:
\
1. temperature_c = the TEMPERATURE from line 1, in degrees C
\
2. pressure_bar = the PRESSURE from line 1, in bar
\
3. the maintenance remaining hours from line 3
\

\
TASK
\
temperature_c = the temperature value on line 1 as a JSON number. Example: if line 1 shows "9.3bar 94C", return 94.
\
temperature_raw = the same temperature as a STRING exactly as displayed, without the C unit.
\
pressure_bar = the pressure value on line 1 as a JSON number. Example: if line 1 shows "9.3bar 94C", return 9.3.
\
pressure_raw = the same pressure as a STRING exactly as displayed, without the bar unit.
\
service_item = the maintenance item name on line 2, in lower case, exactly as shown (for example "oil filter"). If line 2 shows some other maintenance name, still transcribe it exactly - never force it into one of the examples.
\
limit_h = the LEFT hour value on line 3 as a JSON integer (e.g. 2000).
\
remaining_h = the RIGHT hour value on line 3 as a JSON integer (e.g. 1513). Include the minus sign when the value is negative (e.g. -248).
\
remaining_raw = the RIGHT hour value as a STRING exactly as displayed, including any minus sign, without the letter h (e.g. "1513" or "-248").
\

\
RULES
\
- Line 1 always contains pressure and temperature. Read BOTH.
\
- Never swap pressure and temperature. The value followed by bar = pressure_bar. The value followed by C or degrees C = temperature_c.
\
- Keep pressure decimal points. 9.3 is not 93.
\
- Never swap the two hour values. LEFT = interval, RIGHT = remaining.
\
- The letter h is a unit, not a digit.
\
- These are whole service hours: no decimal point.
\
- Unreadable -> null.
\
- Return VALID JSON ONLY. No markdown, no code fences.
\
OUTPUT FORMAT
\
{"temperature_c": <number or null>, "temperature_raw": "<string or null>", "pressure_bar": <number or null>, "pressure_raw": "<string or null>", "service_item": "<text or null>", "limit_h": <int or null>, "remaining_h": <int or null>, "remaining_raw": "<string or null>"}", oiltemp_hmi: "You are an OCR agent. The image shows a machine control panel with a large AMBER / ORANGE
touch-screen HMI. Its rows are labelled in English, for example: Total auto run time (h),
Shot times, Bottle Quantity, Cycle time (s), Production Q'ty (b/h), Planned shot times,
Present shot times, Planned bottle quantity, Preset bottle quantity, plus a "Remaining Time"
block showing hours and minutes.

The value we want is NOT one of those rows. It is in the TOP-RIGHT CORNER of the screen:
a small boxed number immediately followed by its unit written in square brackets as [C].
A "Reset" button sits to its right, and a short mould/product code sits just above it.

TASK
oil_temp     = that top-right boxed number beside [C], as a JSON number, keeping one decimal
               place (e.g. 41.1).
oil_temp_raw = the SAME reading as a STRING exactly as displayed, including the decimal point
               and the digit after it (e.g. "41.1"). Never drop the decimal.
cycle_time   = the "Cycle time" value from the row list (its unit is "s"), transcribed
               separately ONLY so that you do not confuse it with the temperature.
               This value is not recorded.

RULES
- oil_temp is the number beside [C] in the TOP-RIGHT corner. Never a value from the row list.
- Do NOT take Cycle time (unit "s"), Production Q'ty (unit "b/h"), or Remaining Time (h / min).
- Keep the decimal point. 41.1 is not 411. oil_temp_raw must match the display character by character.
- The unit [C] and its brackets are not part of the number.
- Unreadable -> null. Return VALID JSON ONLY. No markdown, no code fences.
OUTPUT FORMAT
{"oil_temp": <number or null>, "oil_temp_raw": "<string or null>", "cycle_time": <number or null>}", oiltemp: "You are an OCR agent. The image shows a machine control panel with a light blue / cyan LCD
screen titled "PRODUCTION MONITOR". The screen lists six labelled rows, top to bottom:
  INTEGRAL TIME      (hours, white digits)
  SHOT COUNTER       (white digits)
  BOTTLE COUNTER     (pcs, white digits)
  CYCLE TIME         (seconds, RED digits)
  BOTTLE PRODUCTION  (BPH, RED digits)
  OIL TEMP.          (degrees C, RED digits)   <-- BOTTOM row, this is the one we want

CRITICAL - read ONLY the value on the BOTTOM row, the one labelled "OIL TEMP.".
Three rows show red digits; OIL TEMP is the LAST of them and the only one followed by C or degrees C.
Do NOT take CYCLE TIME (its unit is "s"). Do NOT take BOTTLE PRODUCTION (its unit is "BPH").

TASK
oil_temp     = the OIL TEMP reading as a JSON number, keeping one decimal place (e.g. 43.8).
oil_temp_raw = the SAME reading as a STRING exactly as displayed, including the decimal point and
               the digit after it (e.g. "43.8"). Never drop the decimal or the trailing digit.
cycle_time   = the CYCLE TIME reading (the row whose unit is "s"), transcribed separately ONLY so
               that you do not confuse it with OIL TEMP. This value is not recorded.

RULES
- Keep the decimal point. 43.8 is not 438. oil_temp_raw must match the display character by character.
- The unit letter C printed beside the number is not part of the number.
- Unreadable -> null. Return VALID JSON ONLY. No markdown, no code fences.
OUTPUT FORMAT
{"oil_temp": <number or null>, "oil_temp_raw": "<string or null>", "cycle_time": <number or null>}", red_dual: "You are an OCR agent. The image shows a control panel with TWO separate red seven-segment displays
side by side. Each has a label above it:
- LEFT display labelled "TEMPERATURE CONTROLLER"
- RIGHT display labelled "ANTI-FREEZE CONTROLLER"

CRITICAL — read ONLY the LEFT display (TEMPERATURE CONTROLLER). Ignore the RIGHT one completely.

The LEFT display also has small static text (e.g. "x5" or tiny labels along the edges) that is NOT
the reading. Do not merge it into the number.

TASK
temp     = the big glowing RED number on the LEFT (TEMPERATURE CONTROLLER) display ONLY, as a JSON number.
temp_raw = the SAME left reading as a STRING exactly as displayed, including the decimal point and
           trailing zero (e.g. "26.7"). Do not drop the decimal.
right_ignored = the RIGHT (ANTI-FREEZE) number, transcribed separately, ONLY so you don't confuse it
           with the left. We do not use it.

- temp is the LEFT display's big glowing number. Never the right one. Never merge small text.
- Keep the decimal point. 26.7 is not 267. temp_raw must match the left display char by char.
- Unreadable -> null. Return VALID JSON ONLY. No markdown, no code fences.
OUTPUT FORMAT
{"temp": <number or null>, "temp_raw": "<string or null>", "right_ignored": <number or null>}", te: "You are an OCR agent. The image shows a blue LCD chiller controller.
The screen has a LARGE white number at the top labelled "PV" (with a small "°C" after it),
and a SMALLER number near the bottom labelled "SET" (the setpoint). Your only job is to TRANSCRIBE.

CRITICAL — there are TWO numbers on this screen:
- PV  = the BIG number at the top. THIS is the one wanted.
- SET = the small number at the bottom next to "SET". This is NOT wanted.
Do not confuse them. Read the big PV number.

TASK
pv     = the BIG "PV" number, as a JSON number.
pv_raw = the same PV reading as a STRING exactly as displayed, including the decimal point
         and any trailing zero (e.g. "22.4"). Do not drop the decimal.
set_val = the small "SET" number, as a JSON number (transcribe it separately so it is not confused with PV).

RULES
- pv is the BIG top number, never the small SET number. Keep the decimal point.
- pv_raw must match the big number char by char.
- Unreadable -> null. Return VALID JSON ONLY. No markdown, no code fences.
OUTPUT FORMAT
{"pv": <number or null>, "pv_raw": "<string or null>", "set_val": <number or null>}", red: "You are an OCR agent. The image shows a single-line RED seven-segment temperature display
(a module labelled "TEMPERATURE CONTROLLER"). There is ONE glowing red number.

CRITICAL — the display has small static text that is NOT the reading:
- a small "x5" or similar mark to the RIGHT of the number
- tiny labels along the bottom edge
Do NOT merge any of that into the number.

TASK
temp     = the big glowing RED number ONLY, as a JSON number. It has a decimal point.
temp_raw = the SAME reading as a STRING exactly as displayed, including the decimal point and
           trailing zero (e.g. "19.0", "20.6"). Do not drop the decimal.
display_raw_text = transcribe EVERYTHING inside the display module left to right (big number first,
           then any small text like "x5"), so the number and the small text are clearly separate.

RULES
- Read only the big glowing digits. Never merge the small "x5" text into the number.
- Keep the decimal point. 19.0 is not 190. temp_raw must match the display char by char.
- Unreadable -> null. Return VALID JSON ONLY. No markdown, no code fences.
OUTPUT FORMAT
{"temp": <number or null>, "temp_raw": "<string or null>", "display_raw_text": "<string>"}", chiller: "You are an OCR agent. The image shows a temperature controller with TWO
seven-segment displays stacked vertically: "PV" on top (GREEN digits), "SV" below (RED digits).

CRITICAL — GHOST DIGITS
An unlit digit position still shows a faint dim outline of "8" because its segments catch light.
A dim/dark/grey "8" is NOT part of the reading — it is an empty position.
Read ONLY the brightly GLOWING digits. Example: dim-8 then bright 3,2 = 32, NOT 832.

TASK
pv     = the number shown by the BRIGHT GREEN glowing digits on the PV display, as a JSON number.
pv_raw = the SAME reading transcribed as a STRING, exactly as it appears on the display,
         INCLUDING any decimal point and trailing zero. If the display shows "29.0", pv_raw is "29.0"
         and pv is 29.0. If it shows "32", pv_raw is "32". Do not drop the decimal in pv_raw.
sv     = the number on the BRIGHT RED glowing digits (SV), as a JSON number.
sv_raw = the SV reading as a STRING, exactly as displayed, including any decimal point.
pv_digits = how many digit positions glow brightly on PV (count each lit digit, ignore the dot).
sv_digits = how many digit positions glow brightly on SV.

RULES
- Read only bright lit digits. Ignore every dim/unlit segment. Never guess.
- pv_raw must match exactly what is printed, char by char (digits + dot). pv is its numeric value.
- Unreadable display -> null for both the number and the raw string.
- Return VALID JSON ONLY. No markdown, no code fences.
OUTPUT FORMAT
{"pv": <number or null>, "pv_raw": "<string or null>", "sv": <number or null>, "sv_raw": "<string or null>", "pv_digits": <int or null>, "sv_digits": <int or null>}", sigma: "You are an OCR agent. The image shows a Kaeser SIGMA CONTROL panel with an LCD
(dark text on a bright yellow-green background). Your only job is to TRANSCRIBE. Do not interpret.

TASK
lcd_lines = transcribe EVERY line on the LCD, exactly as printed, one array entry per line,
            in top-to-bottom order. The first line has a pressure with the unit "bar" attached,
            then a temperature with a degree-Celsius unit. Copy units exactly as printed.

RULES
- Transcribe only what is printed. Never guess. Keep every decimal point. 8.1 is not 81.
- Do not omit any line. Unreadable line -> "?".
- Return VALID JSON ONLY. No markdown, no code fences.
OUTPUT FORMAT
{"lcd_lines": ["<line 1>", "<line 2>", "..."]}", sp100: "You are an OCR agent. The image shows an air compressor with a small LCD
(dark text on a light yellow-green background). Your only job is to TRANSCRIBE. Do not interpret.

TASK
lcd_lines = transcribe EVERY line on the LCD, exactly as printed, one array entry per line.
            The first line starts with "AIR T:" and has a temperature (Celsius) then a voltage
            ending in V — transcribe BOTH. The second line starts with "AIR P:" and has a pressure
            with "BAR". Remaining lines are status text — include them.

RULES
- Transcribe only what is printed. Never guess. Keep every decimal point. 9.7 is not 97.
- Do not omit any line. Unreadable line -> "?".
- Return VALID JSON ONLY. No markdown, no code fences.
OUTPUT FORMAT
{"lcd_lines": ["<line 1>", "<line 2>", "..."]}", booster: "You are an OCR agent. The image shows a Kaeser SIGMA AIR MANAGER BASIC panel.
Your only job is to TRANSCRIBE. Do not interpret.

AREA 1 — top line: "ON AUTO" on the left, then a LARGE pressure value on the right, then "bar".
top_line = transcribe the whole top line exactly, including "ON AUTO" and the value.

AREA 2 — slot row: directly below the top line and its divider, a row of EXACTLY 4 positions,
left to right. Each shows a digit (1,2,3,4) OR a crossed-out X. Below is a row of round icons — IGNORE it.
slot_row = the 4 positions as ONE string separated by single spaces. Digit if a digit shows, X if crossed.
           Read strictly left to right, each position independent. Do NOT assume a pattern.
           Example of FORMAT only (do not copy unless truly seen): "1 2 X X"

RULES
- Transcribe only what is visible at each position. Never guess. Keep the decimal. 31.4 not 314.
- Unreadable slot position -> ? . Return VALID JSON ONLY. No markdown, no code fences.
OUTPUT FORMAT
{"top_line": "<text>", "slot_row": "<4 tokens>"}" };
// ป้ายที่เขียนย่อบนเครื่องจริง -> แปลงเป็นคีย์มาตรฐานก่อนค้น SCREEN
const ALIAS = { '100/1':'SP100/1', '100/2':'SP100/2' };
const AMBIGUOUS = ['PF8','BSD72','SP100','100','COOLING TOWER','ASB250','BOOSTER'];

function norm(s){return String(s==null?'':s).toUpperCase().replace(/\s+/g,' ').trim();}
// ป้ายจริงพิมพ์ไม่เหมือนกันทุกเครื่อง ("PF 8/3" กับ "PF8/7") -> จับคู่แบบตัดช่องว่างทั้งหมด
function tight(s){return norm(s).replace(/\s+/g,'');}
const SCREEN_IX={}; for (const k in SCREEN) SCREEN_IX[tight(k)]={label:k, screen:SCREEN[k]};
const ALIAS_IX={};  for (const k in ALIAS)  ALIAS_IX[tight(k)]=ALIAS[k];
const OILTEMP_IX={};for (const k in OILTEMP_OK) OILTEMP_IX[tight(k)]=k;
const SERVICE_IX={};for (const k in SERVICE_OK) SERVICE_IX[tight(k)]=k;
const AMBIG_IX = AMBIGUOUS.map(tight);
function pickText(j){if(typeof j==='string')return j;let raw='';const pref=['response','text','output','result','content','message','answer','generated_text','data'];for(const k of pref)if(typeof j[k]==='string'&&j[k].length>raw.length)raw=j[k];if(!raw)for(const k of Object.keys(j))if(typeof j[k]==='string'&&j[k].length>raw.length)raw=j[k];return raw;}

const binary = $('ดาวน์โหลดภาพจาก LINE').first().binary;   // เก็บรูปไว้ต่อให้ call 2

const out = [];
for (const item of $input.all()) {
  const raw = pickText(item.json.output || {});
  const blockers = [];
  let label = null, screen = null, promptKey = null, svcFormat = null;

  const _pr = safeJsonParse(raw);
  let parsed = _pr.data;
  if (!_pr.ok) blockers.push(_pr.err);

  if (parsed) {
    const t0 = tight(parsed.machine_label);
    const t  = ALIAS_IX[t0] ? tight(ALIAS_IX[t0]) : t0;   // แปลงป้ายย่อ (100/1 -> SP100/1) ก่อนค้น
    // จอ PRODUCTION MONITOR = รูปใบที่สองของเครื่องเดิม -> เขียนเฉพาะข้อ 2 (อุณหภูมิน้ำมันไฮโดรลิค)
    // ต้องเช็คก่อน SCREEN เพราะป้ายเดียวกัน (เช่น PF8/3) มีได้ 2 จอ แยกด้วยชนิดจอเท่านั้น
    const sk = norm(parsed.screen_kind);
    const isPM  = sk.indexOf('PRODUCTION') !== -1;                       // จอฟ้า PRODUCTION MONITOR
    const isHMI = sk.indexOf('PROFACE') !== -1 || sk.indexOf('HMI') !== -1; // จอส้ม touch-screen
    const isOil = isPM || isHMI;   // ทั้งสองแบบอ่านอุณหภูมิน้ำมัน -> เขียนข้อ 2 เหมือนกัน
    // ---- ตัดสินหน้ารายการซ่อมบำรุงจาก "ข้อความบนจอ" ไม่เชื่อ screen_kind ที่โมเดลตัดสินเอง ----
    // หน้าหลักของ Kaeser (9.3bar 94C | ready) ไม่มีชื่อรายการซ่อมบำรุง -> ต้องไปสาย compressor
    const stight = norm(parsed.screen_text).replace(/\s+/g,'');
    const hasSvcName  = /OILFILTER|OILCHANGE|AIRFILTER|OILSEP[AE]RATOR/.test(stight);
    const hasHourPair = /\d+H[^0-9]{0,8}-?\d+H/.test(stight);
    const hasReset    = stight.indexOf('RESET') !== -1;
    const kaeserByText = hasSvcName && (hasHourPair || hasReset);   // จอ Kaeser: หัวข้อ + คู่ชั่วโมง
    const isUsedPage   = stight.indexOf('BEENUSEDTIME') !== -1;      // จอ SP100: หัว BEEN USED TIME
    // มีข้อความให้ดู -> ใช้ข้อความตัดสิน / ไม่มีเลย -> ค่อยเชื่อ screen_kind เป็นทางสำรอง
    const isSvc = stight
      ? (isUsedPage || kaeserByText)
      : (sk.indexOf('SERVICE') !== -1 || sk.indexOf('KAESER') !== -1);
    const fmt = isUsedPage ? 'beenused' : 'kaeser';   // 2 จอคนละรูปแบบ -> คนละ prompt คนละวิธีเขียน
    if (!t) blockers.push('อ่านตัวระบุไม่ออก — ระบุเครื่องไม่ได้');
    else if (isSvc && SERVICE_IX[t]) {
      label = SERVICE_IX[t]; screen = 'service'; svcFormat = fmt;
      promptKey = (fmt==='beenused') ? 'service_used' : 'service';
    }
    else if (isSvc && AMBIG_IX.indexOf(t) !== -1) blockers.push('ป้าย "'+parsed.machine_label+'" บอกแค่ตระกูล ไม่มีหมายเลข');
    else if (isSvc) blockers.push('หน้ารายการซ่อมบำรุงของ "'+parsed.machine_label+'" ยังไม่รองรับ — ต้องเพิ่มใน SERVICE_OK + CFG ก่อน');
    else if (isOil && OILTEMP_IX[t]) {
      label = OILTEMP_IX[t]; screen = 'oiltemp';
      promptKey = isHMI ? 'oiltemp_hmi' : 'oiltemp';   // จอต่างกัน prompt ต่างกัน
    }
    else if (isOil && AMBIG_IX.indexOf(t) !== -1) blockers.push('ป้าย "'+parsed.machine_label+'" บอกแค่ตระกูล ไม่มีหมายเลข');
    else if (isOil) blockers.push('จอวัดอุณหภูมิน้ำมันของ "'+parsed.machine_label+'" ยังไม่รองรับ — ต้องเพิ่มใน OILTEMP_OK + CFG ก่อน');
    else if (SCREEN_IX[t]) {
      label = SCREEN_IX[t].label; screen = SCREEN_IX[t].screen;
      promptKey = (label==='PF8/7') ? 'red_dual' : screen;   // PF8/7 จอแดงคู่ อ่านจอซ้าย
    }
    else if (AMBIG_IX.indexOf(t) !== -1) blockers.push('ป้าย "'+parsed.machine_label+'" บอกแค่ตระกูล ไม่มีหมายเลข');
    else blockers.push('ป้าย "'+parsed.machine_label+'" ไม่มีในตาราง SCREEN — ต้องเพิ่มก่อน ไม่เดาให้');
  }

  const needs2 = screen ? NEEDS_CALL2[screen] : false;
  out.push({
    json: {
      route: (blockers.length ? 'error' : (ROUTE_OF[screen] || 'error')),
      machine_label: label, screen: screen, needs_call2: needs2, svc_format: svcFormat,
      blockers: blockers,
      message: (screen && needs2) ? (PROMPTS[promptKey] || PROMPTS[screen]) : 'skip',
      call1_raw: raw
    },
    binary: binary
  });
}
return out;
